name: Amazon.com Inc
businessSummary: E-commerce and third-party marketplace retailer; AWS cloud computing; advertising; devices and subscriptions (Prime).

netDebt.note: Total debt $304,841M less cash & investments $114,226M; fulfillment-center lease treatment unconfirmed.

enterpriseValue.note: Mixes Nov price with Sep balance sheet.

fcfTTM.note: Operating CF $168,300M minus capex $215,192M; capex has roughly doubled YoY on AI/data-center buildout.

fcfYield.note: Negative FCF yield -- flag for a GARP screen.

recentEvents: Q3 2025 results: AWS growth reaccelerated; retail and advertising also grew; EPS beat and AWS reacceleration cited as catalysts for a sharp stock rise.
valueTrapFlags: TTM FCF sharply negative (-$46.9B) vs +$7.7B FY2025 and +$32.9B FY2024 -- capex more than doubled for AI/data-center buildout.
Operating cash flow growing (+21% FY2025 to TTM) but entirely outrun by capex -- FCF conversion has collapsed.
No dividend, so payout-based leverage checks n/a.
growthQualityNotes: Revenue growth real, steady, recent: $469.8B (FY2021) to $716.9B (FY2025), ~11%/yr.
Operating margin genuinely expanding: trough 2.6% (FY2022) to 11.15% (FY2025).
Path to sustained positive FCF has REVERSED in the most recent TTM due to the AI capex supercycle -- key watch item.
AMZN absent from the stock-agent feed -- no secondary cross-check available.
dataGaps: Forward P/E, EV/EBIT forward, ND/EBITDA, interest coverage, historical multiple range, itemized forward estimates, stock-agent cross-check unavailable.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS; the sharply negative TTM FCF (AI capex supercycle) is treated as a risk/quality flag rather than built into the basis value

bear.note: AI capex keeps outrunning operating cash flow for longer than expected, margin story stalls.

base.note: AWS reaccelerates as AI capex starts converting to revenue, retail/advertising margins keep expanding.

bull.note: AWS AI infrastructure monetizes faster than expected, FCF reinflects as capex growth moderates.

valuation.whyItFits: Genuine, steady multi-year revenue growth and real operating-margin expansion (2.6% to 11.15%) across retail, advertising and AWS, but the current AI capex supercycle has temporarily reversed free cash flow -- the central open question for this GARP case.
valuation.growthDrivers: AWS AI infrastructure/compute demand, retail logistics efficiency, advertising growth.
valuation.saturation: No saturation in revenue growth; the constraint right now is capital intensity (capex), not demand.
valuation.principalRisk: If AI infrastructure capex does not convert to AWS revenue growth as expected, the current negative free cash flow becomes a structural rather than cyclical problem.
